established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) and agentic LLM systems exhibit hallucination and prompt-injection vulnerabilities that pose concrete risks when applied to operational tasks.
established_findings.evidence_type: Literature survey and empirical vulnerability studies
limitations: Most evidence is from surveys, controlled experiments, and security analyses rather than large-scale production incident datasets.
Severity and frequency of failures depend on deployment architecture (e.g., RAG, tool access) which varies across studies.

established_findings.statement: Augmenting LLMs with tool interfaces, retrieval, validators, and human-in-the-loop gates is a recurring architectural pattern that improves operational safety and auditability in NetOps/AIOps contexts.
limitations: Reported improvements are architectural and qualitative in many papers; quantitative safety gains vary by implementation and are not yet standardized.
Production-readiness claims (e.g., long-term stability) are limited to specific deployments and may not generalize.

established_findings.statement: Constrained decoding and formal constraint-enforcement techniques (CFG-based, integer-programming or grammar-constrained) are viable mitigations to reduce syntactic and constraint violations in model-generated structured outputs.
established_findings.evidence_type: Method papers and decoding technique studies
limitations: Evidence demonstrates feasibility on code/DSL and benchmark tasks; direct evaluations on multi-vendor network configuration DSLs are limited in the supplied records.
Strict constraints can interact poorly with model internal reasoning and may require cascaded or dual-phase designs to preserve semantics.

established_findings.statement: Executable, emulation-grounded benchmarks and closed-loop evaluation (e.g., NetConfArena, OpsEval) reveal that LLM-agent failures in network configuration tasks extend beyond simple command syntax errors and include planning, specification adherence, and execution failures.
limitations: Benchmarks are relatively recent and cover limited task suites; external validity to diverse production topologies and vendor mixes remains to be established.
Different benchmarks use different metrics and hidden tests, complicating direct comparison.

established_findings.statement: Knowledge-graph and graph-based validators can detect inter-command dependency violations and improve validation accuracy compared to unstructured LLM outputs.
limitations: Evaluation results are promising but confined to the datasets and extractors used by the paper; generalization to broader vendor command sets is not shown in the supplied record.
Performance depends on quality of the structured-extraction models and knowledge-graph coverage.

unresolved_questions.statement: How effectively do constrained-decoding and cascaded neuro-symbolic approaches reduce semantic (not only syntactic) misconfigurations across heterogeneous, multi-vendor network DSLs in realistic production topologies?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: Method proposals with limited domain application
limitations: Existing work demonstrates promise on code/DSL benchmarks but lacks direct empirical evaluation on diverse network-device configurations in the supplied records.
Semantic correctness requires deep vendor-specific semantics and cross-command reasoning that current constrained decoders may not fully capture.

unresolved_questions.statement: What is the end-to-end empirical efficacy of generate–verify–repair pipelines (LLM → validator → automated repair loop) in preventing operational outages at scale?
limitations: Supplied records include closed-loop benchmarks and prototypes but do not provide large-scale longitudinal production outage avoidance studies.
Repair efficacy likely depends on validator expressiveness and repair heuristics not standardized in current literature.

unresolved_questions.statement: How transferable are benchmark-derived failure modes (from emulated NetConfArena-like evaluations) to real operator environments with proprietary topologies, noisy telemetry, and human workflows?
limitations: Benchmarks simulate realistic tasks but necessarily abstract certain aspects of production environments (telemetry noise, operator processes, legacy interactions).
Empirical transferability studies are not present in the supplied records.

unresolved_questions.statement: What operational thresholds and human-in-the-loop gating policies optimally balance safety and operator efficiency when allowing LLM-agent proposals to actuate network changes?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: System descriptions noting HITL design choices
limitations: Framework papers discuss HITL gating but do not supply controlled experiments establishing optimal trade-offs.
Optimal thresholds depend on site-specific risk tolerances and are not yet standardized.

candidate_gaps.statement: Standardized, domain-specific evaluation metrics and benchmark suites for RAG/LLM-in-the-loop NetOps (covering semantic correctness, safety, rollbackability, and traceability) are insufficiently developed.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: Survey and benchmark papers noting evaluation shortfalls
limitations: Some benchmarks (NetConfArena, OpsEval) exist but are recent and do not yet constitute a broadly accepted standard.
Cross-benchmark metric harmonization is not yet addressed in the supplied records.

candidate_gaps.statement: Application of grammar-/CFG-constrained or integer-programming constrained decoding specifically tailored to network-device configuration languages (multi-vendor CLI DSLs) remains an under-explored engineering gap.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: Decoding-method papers and general DSL studies
limitations: Decoding techniques have been demonstrated on code/DSL benchmarks; direct application and evaluation on full vendor CLI grammars are not reported in the supplied records.
Building complete grammars for vendor DSLs is engineering-intensive and may require proprietary specifications.

candidate_gaps.statement: Reproducible, openly shared emulation-backed corpora of realistic operator intents, topologies, and failure-injection scenarios for NetOps LLM evaluation are still limited.
limitations: NetConfArena is a step forward but represents a single effort; broader collections and community curation are necessary for coverage across domains and vendors.
Public sharing may be constrained by operator privacy and proprietary topology concerns.

candidate_gaps.statement: Operational threat models for agentic NetOps (including RAG poisoning, tool-poisoning, and registry-level selection biases) require more empirical study and standardized mitigations.
limitations: Existing work documents attack vectors and marketplace design issues, but empirical attack/defense evaluations specifically on NetOps agent pipelines are limited in the supplied records.
Mitigation effectiveness often depends on end-to-end architecture and operational controls.

excluded_claims: Any claim that Batfish or VeriFlow (network-version) was directly used to validate LLM-generated configurations in the supplied records (no supplied record documents Batfish-based LLM validation).

Claims of specific firsts or production-readiness for agentic NetOps beyond the scoped systems described (e.g., blanket statements that any cited framework is production-ready at Internet scale) — such broad production claims are not supported by the supplied records.

Specific numeric failure-rate claims for LLMs on closed-loop NetOps tasks (e.g., exact percent misconfiguration rates across vendor fleets) unless reported explicitly by the referenced benchmark papers (such granular production-wide numbers are not present among the supplied records).

Statements asserting that constrained decoding or CFG methods eliminate semantic misconfigurations entirely — the literature shows reduction in syntactic/constraint violations but not guaranteed semantic correctness.
